topics.title: Winter Math Speed Competition for middle school!
topics.text:
WINTER MATH SPEED COMPETITION!!!!!!!!



UPDATE on the math competition: 

-All signups are CLOSED...

- I have received some competitors' answers.

-Answers are due today by 11:59 Central time

-Results come out around Jan 1, 2017

__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________



I will be hosting a winter math competition for 8th graders, 7th graders, or anyone younger. PLEASE NO older students!!

Anyway, I need 10 competitors NOW FULL, 10 people to help grade, and 10 problem writers. (NOTE: please do one job, not multiple :police: ). Also, if you are planning to sign up, please be devoted and ready to do your task as specified below  :jump:

The test will be 20 questions with 3 tiebreakers, in 20 minutes.



Extra Competition Details:

1) To sign up to be a competitor, grader, or problem writer, you need to comment below which job you would like to do. It will be first come, first serve.

2) Once all the job slots are full, I will contact individually.

3) Note for competitors: please do your best to solve the problems, PLEASE keep the time limit of 20 minutes, do NOT use calculators/aids/etc., and make sure to have fun! Submit your answers in a private message to me by 12/29. Extra info will be sent out

4)Note for people who want to grade:  You will be expected to grade 1 test each by 12/30. I will contact with more grading info.

5)Note for problem writers: You will need to submit 2 questions and their full solutions that are challenging at the middle school level. The problems do not have to be something that can be solved in one minute, despite the time constraint. Please make challenging, mathematical, fun questions for our competitors. Please submit the questions by 12/26 in a private message.

6)placement/top competitors will be announced on jan 1st, 2017



To Sum It Up-- I am hosting math competition, 20 questions in 20 minutes, i need 10 competitors, 10 graders, 10 problem writers, once signups are full i will contact individually :coolspeak:

HAVE FUN everyone!

topics.title: Iniquitous (UPDATED WITH A NEW STANDALONE PROBLEM :D)
topics.text:
So I am making more of this. So yeah.

Head to the bottom of this thread to see the new problems.

Iniquitous

Part 1_____________________________________________________________________________________________

In the grand Ximin system, there was two warring factions battling for control of the bountiful resources: the righteous Crystalbols and the xenophobic Ymirr Horde. The layout of the system is mysterious and intricate one; It follows in the shape of a regular hexagon due to some enigmatic cause deep in the past. The Crystalbols currently control a rectangular shape that passes through the center of the system and is perpendicular to two side and spans the whole length of the system.

Only two of its sides are touching the edges of the dark abyss of space; The two remaining sides act as borders against the Ymirr Horde.

The Ymirr Horde control whatever space they can get, snatching up the rest of the system that the Crystalbols don't control. They are divided in two; Two triangles on the outer parts of this solar system.

What is the ratio of the Crystalbol's (green) area to the Ymirr's area (blue)?

IMAGE

_____________________________________________________________________________________________

Solution(alifenix-)IMAGE

Notice that half of the outlined equilateral triangle ($\tfrac{1}{6}$th of the hexagon) is taken by the Ymirr. $\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{12}$, so each little part is $\tfrac{1}{12}$th of the hexagon.  Therefore,$4$ of those parts makes $\tfrac{1}{3}$.The rest is the Crystalbol's, so they own  of the hexagon. Therefore,$\tfrac{2}{3}$, their ratio is $\frac{\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{1}{3}} = \frac{\frac{2}{3} \cdot 3}{\frac{1}{3} \cdot 3} = \frac{2}{1} = \boxed{2}$.


_____________________________________________________________________________________________

Answer2


_____________________________________________________________________________________________


Part 2 (1/3 FROST Story Arc)On the desolate planet of Rimo 2, where frost and rime regularly fall, where temperatures reach extremes so severe it is almost impossible to comprehend, the Crystalbols were commencing the dastardly FROST project.

The High Command of the Crystalbols have designated a 4 by 4 unit square in the polar region for research and study of REDACTED. They want to deploy a 2 by 2 research command center and 5 ,1 by 1, research outposts. How many ways can they arrange the research command center and research outposts?

_____________________________________________________________________________________________

Solution (alifenix-)We solve this problem in two steps. First, we figure out how many ways we can place the command center, and then after that we can simply "choose" 5 out of the remaining 12 spots to place the research outposts.

IMAGE

See that only in the red squares can you place the upper left block of the command center; otherwise it would leak out of the 4x4 area. Therefore, there are $9$ ways to place the command center. For the research outposts, there are $16 - 2 \cdot 2 = 12$ spots for them. Therefore, we have to choose 5 out of the 12 spots, which therefore is $\binom{12}{5} = \frac{12!}{5! ~ 7!} = \frac{8 \cdot 9 \cdot 10 \cdot 11 \cdot 12}{1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 4 \cdot 5} = 792$ ways to put the research outposts for every way we put the command center. Therefore, there are $792 \cdot 9 = \boxed{7128}$ ways to put them all.


_____________________________________________________________________________________________

Answer7128



Part 3 (2/3 FROST Story Arc)Learning of the FROST Project through their vast network of spies, the Ymirr immediately sent fleets apon fleets to secure this research. Fury shall be upon the poor scientists abandoned by the evacuating guards, be it if they hand over the research to the Ymirr and be hunted down by the Crystalbols or lose trying to protect the data.

However one bright assistant had a idea; they could trap themselves along with the data inside one of the many ice caves on Rimo 2.

The small legion of scientists have trekked to a collection of nearby caves, but they realized that they needed to split up into at least two groups in order to confuse the Ymirr coming after them.

If there are 8 caves and 50 scientists, how many ways can they split up and hide in the caves?

Assume that all the caves are distinguishable and the scientists are not.


Part 4 (3/3 FROST Story Arc)A chuckle rings out from the command deck of a Ymirr scout. It seems like the scientists have locked themselves in the freezer, and now all the Ymirr have to do is retrieve the data.

The scientists have stored all the data inside a small chip in the ice caves, not very wise when you look back on it.

But there was just one problem: The ice caves were being flooded because of all the heat the sudden emergence of the Ymirr has produced. Those hyperdrives sure use a lot of energy.

Now, there is only $70$ minutes before the caves completely flood and the chip is destroyed. The closest Ymirr fleet is comprised of scouts and is $500$ Ymirr units away from Rimo 2. The fleet can travel $200$ Ymirr units per $10$ minutes, and after they reach Rimo 2, they can instantly start slowing the flooding, however they can't stop it or retrieve the data without heavy equipment. They can slow the flooding to only having $\frac{1}{100}$ of the cave being flooded every minute. The second closest fleet is made out of Cruisers who can retrieve the data, and stop the flooding, but they are $1000$ Ymirr units away and can travel at the speed of $100$ Ymirr Units per $15$ minutes.

Will the Ymirr be successful at retrieving the data collected from the FROST Project?
